blocks.content: Manipur's polity chapter follows the standard state structure but includes a distinctive Hill Areas administrative framework reflecting the valley-hills divide from Chapter 1, plus the state's very recent, highly consequential experience of President's Rule (2025-26).

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Manipur's Assembly has 20 ST-reserved seats but NO SC-reserved seats — distinct from most Indian states, reflecting Manipur's very small Scheduled Caste population relative to its large Scheduled Tribe population.
President's Rule, 2025-2026: A Recent, Significant Episode

Following nearly two years of serious ethnic violence in the state (beginning May 2023, detailed with appropriate care in Chapter 12), Chief Minister N. Biren Singh resigned on 9 February 2025, shortly before his government was due to face a no-confidence motion; with no alternative government able to be formed, President's Rule was imposed under Article 356 of the Constitution on 13 February 2025.

President's Rule was extended by Parliament in six-month blocks (as constitutionally required) through 2025, with the state administered directly by Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla — a former Union Home Secretary with a background in the Assam-Meghalaya cadre — during this period, with joint security forces conducting operations aimed at restoring law and order.

President's Rule was revoked on 4 February 2026, when Yumnam Khemchand Singh (a BJP MLA and former Assembly Speaker, from a faction within the party distinct from former CM N. Biren Singh) was sworn in as the state's 13th Chief Minister, heading a deliberately inclusive coalition cabinet featuring Deputy Chief Ministers from both the Kuki-Zo and Naga communities — a structural attempt to signal broad-based, cross-community government following the preceding period of ethnic conflict.

cells: Chief Minister N. Biren Singh resigns, shortly before a scheduled no-confidence motion
President's Rule imposed under Article 356; Assembly kept under suspended animation (not dissolved)
President's Rule extended by Parliament in six-month blocks, as constitutionally required
President's Rule revoked; Yumnam Khemchand Singh sworn in as 13th Chief Minister, with Deputy CMs Nemcha Kipgen (Kuki-Zo) and Losii Dikho (Naga)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: This is a genuinely recent and significant current-affairs sequence — remember the key structural fact that the Manipur Legislative Assembly was kept under SUSPENDED ANIMATION (not dissolved) throughout the 2025-26 President's Rule period, meaning the same Assembly (elected in 2022, with a term until March 2027) resumed functioning once President's Rule was revoked, rather than requiring fresh elections.

items: Reflecting the valley-hills divide (Chapter 1), Manipur's hill districts are administered under a distinct framework — the Manipur (Hill Areas) District Councils Act, 1971, providing for elected Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) in the hill districts, intended to give hill-area tribal communities a degree of local self-governance over specified subjects, broadly analogous in spirit (though more limited in scope) to the Sixth Schedule councils of other North-Eastern states.

The precise scope, funding and functioning of these Hill Area District Councils has been a recurring subject of political debate and demand for reform, particularly from hill-based political and civil-society organisations seeking greater autonomy — a theme connected to the wider identity-politics context of Chapter 12.
60-seat unicameral Assembly: 20 ST-reserved seats, no SC-reserved seats.
Current Governor (2026): Ajay Kumar Bhalla (since 3 Jan 2025). Current CM: Yumnam Khemchand Singh (BJP), 13th CM, since 4 Feb 2026.
Deputy CMs: Nemcha Kipgen (Kuki-Zo, Manipur's first woman Deputy CM) and Losii Dikho (Naga, NPF) — a deliberately inclusive cabinet.
President's Rule: imposed 13 Feb 2025 (after N. Biren Singh's 9 Feb 2025 resignation); Assembly kept in suspended animation (not dissolved); revoked 4 Feb 2026.
Manipur (Hill Areas) District Councils Act, 1971 provides for Autonomous District Councils in the hill districts.
